Android TV, like Google TV, still too ahead of its time

As an owner of the NSZ-GT1, here are the problems I ran into as a Google TV owner.

  • Tons of apps which would have worked absolutely fine were not available because they needed to be set as available.
  • Sideloading was a royal pain in the ass.
  • There was no 'Nexus' version; there was no easy way to root and customize. There were no custom roms. I feel this is incredibly important to a device (or specialized OS) making it to that adoption stage for the general public - people doing weird fun crap with it.
  • Sony was piss-poor at updating, and dropped support far too quickly.

It still works, but my Roku does a better job. It could have been great if Sony were open with their NSZ-GT1 like they are with their Z series of phones. I wish they would just open it up now so I could breathe new life into it besides being a blu-ray player.

I think Android TV is here to stay. Is it perfect in its current form? No. Does it have potential to evolve into something great? You bet your ass.

What Google needs to focus on now is refinement and developer outreach. As far as refining the platform, something I think we all want is for Search to get smarter. As of right now, unless I am mistaken (it's been awhile since I've tried it), if you do a voice search for Breaking Bad while on the home screen, the only results that are displayed are ones from a Google Play source. Problem is, I already pay for Netflix, and would rather the system display content that is relevant to the service that I am already paying for. I think that if Google can eventually nail this down, Android TV will become immensely useful, and it will drastically set itself apart from the other Set Top Box platforms. There are other little nitpick things that I am sure will eventually get address. These involve rearranging the home screen, allowing for multiple Google Play accounts under one device, etc, etc.

As far as outreach goes, while the number of Android TV optimized apps are growing every day, there is still an alarming amount of big media apps that do not support the platform. HBO Go & Now for example, while available on tablets and phones, are still not accessible via the Android TV interface. Fortunately, Go users can cast their content thanks to Google Cast, but the primary reason I purchased a Nexus Player was because I wanted to maintain a leanback experience with a remote in hand.
